Slice: Extend Loan

Intent

Let a borrower keep a tool longer by extending their loan from My Loans. An extension moves the due date later by one of the tool's default checkout periods. It is refused while someone is waiting for the tool, once the loan is overdue, while the borrower is suspended, and once the tool has been retired.

Trigger & Actor

The borrower, from the My Loans screen, on one of their own loans that My Loans offers Extend on. How the system recognises the borrower is the open identity question in Add Tool (slices/add-tool.md); this slice follows its answer.

Command / Input

Command: Extend Loan

A LoanId is a UUID. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone. "Today" is that date at the moment the command is handled.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor extending, who must be the one making the request and the loan's borrower (INV-EXT-1).
loanId LoanId yes The loan to extend. Must be a loan that has been checked out (INV-EXT-9).
fromDueDate Date yes The due date the borrower is extending from, as My Loans showed it. Must be the loan's current due date, unless this exact extension has already been recorded (INV-EXT-10).

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Loans @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Loan Extended → context Loans Read by: My Loans, Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (the new due date shown); Overdue Loans To Notify and Neighbors To Flag (when the loan becomes overdue, and whether a return is late); Undelivered Notices and Flagged Neighbors (loan details shown there).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command.
fromDueDate Date yes From the command: the loan's due date before this extension.
dueDate Date yes Set by the system: the new due date, fromDueDate plus the tool's default checkout period (INV-EXT-3).
extendedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

A later extension records a new Loan Extended; this one never changes. A loan's current due date is the dueDate of its latest Loan Extended, or of its Tool Checked Out if it has never been extended.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Loan Extended moves the loan's due date in My Loans, Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog, and in the lists that work out overdue loans and late returns. Each view is specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-EXT-1: Only the borrower can extend a loan, and they do it themselves.
    • The command names the acting neighbor in neighborId. The request must come from that neighbor (requester-mismatch), and the loan must be theirs: the neighbor who checked the tool out (not-your-loan). How the requester is recognised is the open identity question.
  • INV-EXT-2: Only an open loan can be extended.
    • A loan is open from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan.
  • INV-EXT-3: An extension adds one of the tool's default checkout periods to the loan's current due date.
    • It adds the tool's default period even if the borrower chose a shorter period at checkout.
    • The default period is the one on Tool Added. It never changes.
  • INV-EXT-4: An extension is refused while any hold is waiting on the tool.
    • A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, the holder checks the tool out, the tool is retired or recorded lost, or the holder closes their account. This is the meaning the Tool Catalog and Place Hold use.
    • My Loans shows the same (INV-MYL-9), except for a moment it can't see: when a lapsed set-aside has gone to the next holder and its Hold Expired isn't recorded yet. My Loans then holds back Extend for a few seconds; this slice already allows it.
    • Holds that were already waiting when the loan began count too.
  • INV-EXT-5: An extension is refused once the loan is overdue.
    • A loan is overdue from the start of the day after its current due date, in the shed's local time. On the due date itself, the loan can still be extended.
    • Only the overdue loan itself is refused. The same borrower can still extend their other loans that are not overdue.
  • INV-EXT-6: There is no limit on how many times a loan can be extended, as long as each extension meets the other rules here.
  • INV-EXT-7: A suspended neighbor can't extend a loan.
    • A neighbor is suspended from Neighbor Suspended until Neighbor Reinstated. Once reinstated, they can extend again.
    • A closed account has no open loans, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan, so it needs no rule here.
  • INV-EXT-8: A loan whose tool has been retired can't be extended.
    • The loan carries on until the tool is returned or recorded lost.
  • INV-EXT-9: The loan must exist.
  • INV-EXT-10: Extending from a due date that has already been extended from adds nothing.
    • A repeated request succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the loan since. A request whose fromDueDate is neither the loan's current due date nor one it has already been extended from is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana has the cordless drill on loan L1. The drill has a 7-day default checkout period. L1 is due 12 October, has never been extended, and no hold is waiting on the drill. Ana is active, and today is 10 October.

  • Happy path (INV-EXT-3)
    • Given: L1 as above
    • When: Ana extends L1 from My Loans, from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded for L1, from 12 October to 19 October.
  • Extending on the due date (INV-EXT-5)
    • Given: today is 12 October
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, to 19 October.
  • Extending the day after the due date (INV-EXT-5)
    • Given: today is 13 October, and L1 is still due 12 October
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1 from 12 October
    • Then: refused with loan-overdue: "This loan is overdue and can't be extended. Please return the tool." No event is recorded.
  • Extending again (INV-EXT-6)
    • Given: L1 has already been extended once and is due 19 October; today is 18 October
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 19 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, from 19 October to 26 October.
  • Extending a loan checked out for a shorter period (INV-EXT-3)
    • Given: Ana checked out the drill for 3 days, so L1 is due 8 October; today is 7 October
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 8 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, to 15 October: the drill's 7-day default, not 3 days.
  • A hold is waiting (INV-EXT-4)
    • Given: Ben has placed a hold on the drill, and it is still waiting
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with hold-waiting: "Someone is waiting for this tool, so this loan can't be extended." No event is recorded.
  • A hold was waiting when the loan began (INV-EXT-4)
    • Given: Ana checked out the drill as the front holder, and Cara's hold was behind hers and is still waiting
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with hold-waiting.
  • The waiting hold has ended (INV-EXT-4)
    • Given: Ben placed a hold on the drill, and then cancelled it
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, to 19 October.
  • Another of the borrower's loans is overdue (INV-EXT-5)
    • Given: Ana also has the ladder on loan, due 4 October, so it is overdue
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded for L1, to 19 October. The ladder loan is still overdue.
  • Suspended borrower (INV-EXT-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't extend loans while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Reinstated borrower (INV-EXT-7)
    • Given: Ana was suspended and has been reinstated
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, to 19 October.
  • Tool retired while on loan (INV-EXT-8)
    • Given: the drill was retired while Ana has it on loan
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with tool-retired: "This tool has been retired, so this loan can't be extended. Please return it by the due date." No event is recorded.
  • Loan already returned (INV-EXT-2)
    • Given: Ana has returned the drill, ending L1
    • When: a request to extend L1 from 12 October arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-ended: "This loan has ended." No event is recorded.
  • Loan ended by loss (INV-EXT-2)
    • Given: Tool Lost has been recorded for L1
    • When: a request to extend L1 arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-ended.
  • Unknown loan (INV-EXT-9)
    • Given: no loan L9 has been checked out
    • When: a request to extend L9 arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else's loan (INV-EXT-1)
    • Given: L1 is Ana's loan
    • When: Ben, naming himself, tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with not-your-loan: "You can only extend your own loans." No event is recorded.
  • A request that doesn't come from the neighbor it names (INV-EXT-1)
    • Given: L1 is Ana's loan
    • When: a request to extend L1, naming Ana, comes from someone other than Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only extend loans for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-EXT-10)
    • Given: Loan Extended was recorded for L1, from 12 October to 19 October
    • When: the same request to extend L1 from 12 October arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. L1 is still due 19 October.
  • The same request after a hold was placed (INV-EXT-10)
    • Given: Loan Extended was recorded for L1, from 12 October to 19 October, and Ben has since placed a hold on the drill
    • When: the same request to extend L1 from 12 October arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Extending from a due date that isn't current (INV-EXT-10)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October and has never been extended
    • When: a request to extend L1 from 5 October arrives
    • Then: refused with due-date-changed: "This loan's due date has changed. Check it and try again." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the borrower on the My Loans screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. requester-mismatch (INV-EXT-1).
  2. loan-not-found (INV-EXT-9).
  3. not-your-loan (INV-EXT-1).
  4. If a Loan Extended for this loan already has the same fromDueDate, the request is a repeat: it succeeds and records nothing (INV-EXT-10).
  5. loan-ended (INV-EXT-2).
  6. due-date-changed, if fromDueDate isn't the loan's current due date (INV-EXT-10).
  7. neighbor-suspended (INV-EXT-7).
  8. tool-retired (INV-EXT-8).
  9. loan-overdue (INV-EXT-5).
  10. hold-waiting (INV-EXT-4).
Reason Sentence Rule
requester-mismatch You can only extend loans for yourself. INV-EXT-1
loan-not-found There is no such loan. INV-EXT-9
not-your-loan You can only extend your own loans. INV-EXT-1
loan-ended This loan has ended. INV-EXT-2
due-date-changed This loan's due date has changed. Check it and try again. INV-EXT-10
neighbor-suspended You can't extend loans while your account is suspended. INV-EXT-7
tool-retired This tool has been retired, so this loan can't be extended. Please return it by the due date. INV-EXT-8
loan-overdue This loan is overdue and can't be extended. Please return the tool. INV-EXT-5
hold-waiting Someone is waiting for this tool, so this loan can't be extended. INV-EXT-4

loan-not-found and requester-mismatch can only come from a faulty or impersonating caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed loan ID (not a UUID), or a fromDueDate that isn't a date, is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: each extension is identified by the loan and the due date it extends from. A double submit, or a retry after a lost response, carries the same fromDueDate, so it succeeds with nothing recorded, even if the loan has since changed. It never extends the loan twice.

Two requests for the same loan at the same moment: each is decided against the loan's events as already recorded, one at a time, so only one Loan Extended is recorded from a given due date.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the borrower may extend their own loan (INV-EXT-1). The shed manager doesn't extend loans. How the requester is recognised is the open identity question in Add Tool.
  • PII & compliance: Loan Extended holds only the loan and its dates. No name or email.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate, checkedOutAt.
    • Loan Extended (this slice): loanId, fromDueDate, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool), Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor), Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold), Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/add-tool.md, check-out-tool.md, tool-inventory.md and tool-catalog.md. This slice adds fromDueDate and extendedAt to Loan Extended; readers that only need the new due date keep reading {loanId, dueDate}.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Loans, Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, Overdue Loans To Notify, Neighbors To Flag, Undelivered Notices and Flagged Neighbors (the new due date).

Open Questions

  • How a person is recognised (the identity question) — brief 10 A1. The requester checks here follow its answer.
"},{"index":4,"name":"Cancel Hold","x0":796.76,"x1":940.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Cancel Hold

Intent

Let a neighbor give up a hold they no longer want, from My Holds, so the tool goes to the next neighbor in the queue instead of waiting on them. A hold can be cancelled while it is waiting or while the tool is set aside for the holder, and a suspended neighbor can cancel too.

What follows a cancellation is decided by the views and slices that read Hold Cancelled:

  • Every hold behind the cancelled one on that tool moves up one place (My Holds, Holds To Fulfill).
  • Cancelling a hold that is ready for pickup ends the set-aside. The tool passes to the next hold, or becomes available if none is waiting (Holds To Fulfill, Tool Catalog), the same as when a set-aside expires.
  • A cancelled hold gives up its place for good. The neighbor may place a new hold on the same tool, which joins the back of the queue (Place Hold, INV-HOLD-7: only a live hold counts).

Trigger & Actor

The holder, from the My Holds screen, on one of their own holds that hasn't ended. The shed manager doesn't cancel holds. How the system recognises the holder is the open identity question in Add Tool (slices/add-tool.md); this slice follows its answer.

Command / Input

Command: Cancel Hold

A HoldId or NeighborId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
holdId HoldId yes The hold to cancel. Must be a hold that has been placed (INV-CNH-7).
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor cancelling, who must be the one making the request (requester-mismatch) and the hold's holder (not-your-hold) (INV-CNH-1).

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Holds @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Hold Cancelled → context Holds Read by: My Holds and Tool Catalog (their continuations right after this slice), My Loans (whether a hold is still waiting on a borrowed tool), Holds To Fulfill and Pickups To Expire (the hold's queue and set-aside), Pickup Notices To Send (no pickup email for a cancelled set-aside), and Undelivered Notices (a failed pickup email's entry drops off).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
holdId HoldId yes From the command. The tool and holder are those on the hold's Hold Placed.
cancelledAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

The event doesn't say whether the hold was waiting or set aside. Readers already know from Hold Placed and Hold Fulfilled.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Hold Cancelled ends the hold in My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans and the hold to-do lists, each specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-CNH-1: A neighbor can cancel only their own hold, and does it themselves.
    • The command names the acting neighbor in neighborId. The request must come from that neighbor (requester-mismatch), and the hold must be theirs (not-your-hold). The shed manager does not cancel holds. How the requester is recognised is the open identity question.
  • INV-CNH-2: A hold can be cancelled while it is waiting or while the tool is set aside for the holder.
    • A suspended neighbor may cancel their own hold. Cancelling only gives up their own claim.
    • A set-aside whose collect-by date has passed, but whose Hold Expired hasn't been recorded yet, hasn't ended, so it can still be cancelled. Either way the tool passes on.
  • INV-CNH-3: A hold that has ended in any way other than being cancelled can't be cancelled.
    • A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, the holder checks the tool out, the tool is retired or recorded lost, or the holder closes their account.
    • A hold the holder has already cancelled is covered by INV-CNH-8.
  • INV-CNH-7: The hold must exist.
  • INV-CNH-8: Cancelling a hold that is already cancelled succeeds and records nothing new.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never fails and never records a second Hold Cancelled.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ben and Cara are active neighbors, and Ben's hold H1 on the cordless drill was placed before Cara's hold H2.

  • Cancel a waiting hold (INV-CNH-2)
    • Given: the drill is checked out by Ana, and H1 and H2 are waiting
    • When: Ben cancels H1 from My Holds
    • Then: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1.
  • Cancel a hold that is ready for pickup (INV-CNH-2)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben under H1, with a collect-by date of 17 October, and H2 is waiting
    • When: Ben cancels H1 on 15 October
    • Then: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1.
  • Cancel a lapsed set-aside before its expiry is recorded (INV-CNH-2)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben under H1, to collect by 17 October. It is 18 October and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded for H1.
    • When: Ben cancels H1
    • Then: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1, and no Hold Expired follows for it.
  • Suspended neighbor cancels a hold (INV-CNH-2)
    • Given: Ben is suspended, and H1 is waiting
    • When: Ben cancels H1
    • Then: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-CNH-8)
    • Given: Hold Cancelled has been recorded for H1
    • When: the same request to cancel H1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • A request that doesn't come from the neighbor it names (INV-CNH-1)
    • Given: H1 is Ben's waiting hold
    • When: a request to cancel H1, naming Ben, comes from someone other than Ben
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only cancel holds for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else's hold (INV-CNH-1)
    • Given: H1 is Ben's waiting hold
    • When: Cara, naming herself, tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with not-your-hold: "You can only cancel your own holds." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown hold (INV-CNH-7)
    • Given: no hold H9 has been placed
    • When: a request to cancel H9 arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-not-found: "There is no such hold." No event is recorded.
  • Hold already expired (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: Hold Expired has been recorded for H1
    • When: Ben tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended: "This hold has already ended." No event is recorded.
  • Hold ended by the holder's checkout (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: Ben checked out the drill as H1's holder, which ended H1
    • When: Ben tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Hold ended by retirement (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: the drill was retired while H1 was waiting
    • When: Ben tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Hold ended because the tool was recorded lost (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: Tool Lost was recorded for Ana's loan of the drill while H1 was waiting
    • When: Ben tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Hold ended by closing the account (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: Ben closed his account while H1 was waiting
    • When: a request to cancel H1 for Ben arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on the My Holds screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. requester-mismatch (INV-CNH-1).
  2. hold-not-found (INV-CNH-7).
  3. not-your-hold (INV-CNH-1).
  4. If Hold Cancelled is already recorded for the hold, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-CNH-8).
  5. hold-ended (INV-CNH-3).
Reason Sentence Rule
requester-mismatch You can only cancel holds for yourself. INV-CNH-1
hold-not-found There is no such hold. INV-CNH-7
not-your-hold You can only cancel your own holds. INV-CNH-1
hold-ended This hold has already ended. INV-CNH-3

hold-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. hold-not-found is worded the same wherever a hold is looked up.

Idempotency: cancelling is safe to repeat (INV-CNH-8). A repeat records nothing, whatever has happened since.

Requests at the same moment: each cancellation is decided against the hold's events as already recorded, one at a time per hold. If the holder cancels just as the hold ends another way (the fulfiller sets the tool aside, the expirer expires it, or the tool is retired), whichever is recorded first stands. A cancel decided after an expiry, retirement or closure is refused with hold-ended. A cancel decided after Hold Fulfilled cancels the set-aside.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Cancelling sends no email.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the holder may cancel their own hold (INV-CNH-1). How the requester is recognised is the open identity question in Add Tool.
  • PII & compliance: Hold Cancelled holds only the hold's ID and a time. No name or email.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (this slice): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): toolId, neighborId (the holder's own checkout ends their hold on that tool).
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, matched to the tool through Tool Checked Out.loanId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/place-hold.md, check-out-tool.md and tool-catalog.md. Hold Cancelled adds cancelledAt; readers that need only {holdId} are unaffected.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire, Pickup Notices To Send and Undelivered Notices. Place Hold accepts a new hold from the same neighbor on the same tool once this one is cancelled.

Open Questions

  • How a person is recognised (the identity question) — brief 10 A1. The requester checks here follow its answer.
"},{"index":5,"name":"Record Overdue Notice Failure","x0":965.76,"x1":1109.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Record Overdue Notice Failure

Intent

Record that an overdue notice could not be delivered to the borrower, so the shed manager knows the neighbor wasn't told and can follow up in person, and the borrower's My Loans shows that the notice didn't reach them.

Trigger & Actor

Externally triggered. The email provider, outside the shed, sends a final failure report for an overdue notice the shed handed it. The Email Provider Failure Report translation turns that report into the Record Overdue Notice Failure command. No person records a failure, and there is no screen.

What the report carries: the reference the shed gave the notice when it handed it over, which is the loan's ID, since each loan gets at most one overdue notice; and the reason, refused or bounced. Anything else in the report, such as the email address, is not recorded.

Command / Input

Command: Record Overdue Notice Failure

A LoanId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
loanId LoanId yes The reference from the provider's report: the loan the notice was about. Must match an Overdue Notice Sent (INV-ONF-7), for a loan that hasn't ended (INV-ONF-8).
reason Text yes refused or bounced, from the report (INV-ONF-3). Any other value is bad input.

Trigger

Triggered by: translation Email Provider Failure Report, also in this slice (externally triggered by the email provider's final failure report).

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Overdue Notice Failed → context Loans Read by: My Loans (the loan shows the notice couldn't be delivered) and Undelivered Notices (the shed manager's follow-up list).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command.
reason Text yes From the command: refused or bounced.
failedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the failure date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

The event never changes. No later event retries the notice or clears the failure.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Overdue Notice Failed feeds two views, each specified in its own doc:

  • My Loans (slices/my-loans.md) shows the borrower that the overdue notice couldn't be delivered.
  • Undelivered Notices (slices/undelivered-notices.md) lists the failure for the shed manager to follow up.

Both are eventually consistent. Overdue Loans To Notify doesn't hear this event: the loan left that list when Overdue Notice Sent was recorded.

Invariants / Business Rules

Every recorded failure is shown to the shed manager on Undelivered Notices, and to the borrower on My Loans; those views own how it is shown.

A failure is recorded only from the email provider's report; no person records it, and the only way in is the translation in Trigger & Actor. The shed records only the provider's one final failure report: the provider makes 3 delivery attempts over about an hour and reports a final failure only if all of them fail. The shed does no retrying of its own, and a failure a later attempt recovers from is never reported. How the provider's link to the shed is secured is part of the email port contract proposed for the constitution (brief 10, A5).

  • INV-ONF-3: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for the loan the notice was about, with the moment of the failure and whether the email was refused or bounced.
    • Refused and bounced are the two reasons the provider's final report can give.
  • INV-ONF-4: Every Overdue Notice Failed follows an Overdue Notice Sent for the same loan.
    • Overdue Notice Sent is recorded at hand-off, so the loan has already left Overdue Loans To Notify. Recording the failure doesn't change that list.
  • INV-ONF-6: A loan has at most one Overdue Notice Failed. No further notice is attempted for it after a failure.
    • The shed manager follows up in person.
  • INV-ONF-7: A failure report that matches no overdue notice the shed sent is ignored, and nothing is recorded.
  • INV-ONF-8: A failure report that arrives after the loan has ended, because the tool was returned or recorded lost, is ignored, and nothing is recorded.
    • For example, the borrower returned the tool during the hour the provider spent retrying.
  • INV-ONF-9: A failure report repeated for a loan whose failure is already recorded, with the same reason, succeeds and records nothing new. With a different reason it is ignored, and nothing is recorded.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Refused (INV-ONF-3)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for Ana's drill loan L1, and the drill is still out
    • When: the provider's final report says the notice for L1 was refused
    • Then: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1, reason refused, with the time it was recorded. No further notice is sent for L1.
  • Bounced (INV-ONF-3)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and the drill is still out
    • When: the provider's final report says the notice for L1 bounced
    • Then: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1, reason bounced.
  • Report matching no notice (INV-ONF-4, INV-ONF-7)
    • Given: no Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for loan L2
    • When: a failure report names L2
    • Then: ignored with no-matching-notice. Nothing is recorded.
  • Report arrives after the tool was returned (INV-ONF-8)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and Tool Returned was then recorded for L1 while the provider was still retrying
    • When: the provider's final report says the notice for L1 bounced
    • Then: ignored with loan-ended. Nothing is recorded.
  • Report arrives after the tool was recorded lost (INV-ONF-8)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and Tool Lost was then recorded for L1
    • When: the provider's final report says the notice for L1 was refused
    • Then: ignored with loan-ended. Nothing is recorded.
  • The same report arrives twice (INV-ONF-6, INV-ONF-9)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Failed was recorded for L1, reason bounced
    • When: the same report, L1 bounced, arrives again
    • Then: it succeeds and nothing new is recorded. L1 still has one Overdue Notice Failed.
  • A second report with a different reason (INV-ONF-6, INV-ONF-9)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Failed was recorded for L1, reason bounced
    • When: a report arrives saying the notice for L1 was refused
    • Then: ignored with failure-already-recorded. Nothing is recorded; L1 keeps its one failure, reason bounced.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: a stable name and a sentence. No person sees these; they go back to the translation, which takes no further action, and are kept for diagnosing the provider link.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. no-matching-notice (INV-ONF-7).
  2. A failure already recorded for the loan (INV-ONF-9): a repeat with the same reason succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise failure-already-recorded.
  3. loan-ended (INV-ONF-8).
Reason Sentence Rule
no-matching-notice No overdue notice was sent for that loan. INV-ONF-7
failure-already-recorded A failure is already recorded for that notice. INV-ONF-9
loan-ended That loan has already ended. INV-ONF-8

A missing or malformed loan ID, or a reason other than refused or bounced, is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: the provider may deliver the same final report more than once. A repeat with the same loan and reason succeeds and records nothing new, even if the loan has since ended. So one failure never shows twice on Undelivered Notices.

Retries and compensations: none in the shed. The provider's own 3 attempts happen before its final report. After a failure no further notice is attempted; following up is the shed manager's job, in person.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the email provider's failure report can trigger this command, through the translation. How the shed checks a report really comes from its provider is part of the email port contract proposed for the constitution (brief 10, A5).
  • PII & compliance: Overdue Notice Failed holds no name or email: only the loan, the reason and the time. The address the notice went to is already on Overdue Notice Sent (sentTo), so the email address in the provider's report is not recorded again.
  • Performance / SLA: none. A failure shows on Undelivered Notices shortly after the report arrives, about an hour after the notice was handed over.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice): loanId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Overdue Notice Failed (this slice): loanId, reason.
    • Overdue Notice Sent, and the loan's ID as the reference the provider quotes back, match slices/send-overdue-notice.md. Return Tool and Record Tool Lost are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Loans and Undelivered Notices (the failure).

Open Questions

  • How the provider's failure reports are secured: part of the email port contract (brief 10 A5).
"},{"index":6,"name":"Undelivered Notices","x0":1134.76,"x1":1278.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Undelivered Notices

Intent

Shows the shed manager every email the shed couldn't deliver — overdue notices and pickup notices — so they can reach the neighbor another way. A neighbor who wasn't told their loan is overdue, or that a tool is waiting for them, doesn't stay unnoticed. An entry stays only while there is something to follow up.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Undelivered Notices screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per failed overdue notice whose loan is still open, and one per failed pickup notice whose set-aside hasn't ended, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. The screen offers no actions. Following up is the shed manager's job, in person; no email is tried again after its failure is recorded (Send Overdue Notice, INV-OVN-9).
  • Which failure reports become events is decided by the two failure slices: a report that matches no notice the shed sent, or that arrives after the loan or set-aside has ended, is ignored there and never reaches this view.

Read Model / View

  • View: Undelivered Notices built from events: "Overdue Notice Failed", "Pickup Notice Failed", "Tool Added", "Neighbor Registered", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Tool Returned", "Tool Lost", "Hold Fulfilled", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Expired", "Tool Retired", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the Undelivered Notices screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. An entry appears, changes or drops off shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes).

One row per entry. LoanId, HoldId, ToolId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be empty.

Field Type Source / Notes
kind Text overdue-notice or pickup-notice. Derived: from which failure event created the entry.
loanId LoanId Optional; overdue-notice entries only. Overdue Notice Failed.loanId.
holdId HoldId Optional; pickup-notice entries only. Derived: Pickup Notice Failed.holdId.
neighborId NeighborId The borrower (Tool Checked Out.neighborId for the loan) or the holder (Hold Fulfilled.neighborId for the hold).
neighborName Text Derived: Neighbor Registered.name for neighborId.
neighborEmail Text Derived: Neighbor Registered.email for neighborId, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email. Always the current one.
toolId ToolId Tool Checked Out.toolId for the loan, or Hold Fulfilled.toolId for the hold.
toolName Text Derived: Tool Added.name for toolId.
dueDate Date Optional; overdue-notice entries only. Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for the loan.
collectByDate Date Optional; pickup-notice entries only. Derived: Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate for the hold.
reason Text refused or bounced, from the failure event's reason.
failedAt Instant From the failure event's failedAt. Shown as the failure date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

To fill an entry the moment its failure lands, the view also keeps, for every open loan, its tool, borrower and current due date, and for every live set-aside, its tool, holder and collect-by date. These are bookkeeping, not rows, and are never returned.

When an entry drops off.

  • An overdue-notice entry drops off when its loan ends: Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan. Retiring the tool while it is out doesn't end the loan, so the entry stays.
  • A pickup-notice entry drops off when its set-aside ends: the holder checks the tool out (Tool Checked Out for that tool and holder), or Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for the hold, or Tool Retired for the tool, or Neighbor Account Closed for the holder.

Nothing brings an entry back.

Queries

  • List undelivered notices. Takes nothing. Returns every entry with all the fields above. There is no paging. The order is the shared list-order question in .event-modeling.md (Open questions); under its recommendation entries are listed by neighbor name, then by failedAt.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-UDN-1: Every Overdue Notice Failed and every Pickup Notice Failed creates exactly one entry.
    • Nothing else creates an entry. A failure is recorded only after the email provider has made its 3 delivery attempts over about an hour and reported a final failure, so the shed manager never sees a notice that is still being tried.
  • INV-UDN-2: Each entry shows the failure date, and whether the provider refused the email or it bounced.
    • A bounce usually means a wrong email address. The shed manager can ask the neighbor to change it from My Account.
  • INV-UDN-3: An overdue-notice entry shows the borrower's name and current email, the tool's name, and the loan's current due date.
    • The name comes from Neighbor Registered, the email from Neighbor Registered as replaced by any Neighbor Email Changed, the tool's name from Tool Added, and the due date from Tool Checked Out as moved by any Loan Extended.
  • INV-UDN-3a: A pickup-notice entry shows the holder's name and current email, the tool's name, and the collect-by date.
    • The collect-by date is the one recorded on Hold Fulfilled. Name, email and tool name come from the same events as for an overdue-notice entry.
  • INV-UDN-4: An overdue-notice entry drops off when its loan ends: the tool is returned, or the shed manager records it lost.
    • Either way the loan has ended, and there is nothing left to follow up. A tool retired while out keeps its entry until one of these happens.
  • INV-UDN-5: A pickup-notice entry drops off when its set-aside ends.
    • A set-aside ends when the holder collects the tool, or the hold is cancelled or expires, or it ends because the tool was retired or the holder closed their account.
  • INV-UDN-8: Applying the same event twice leaves Undelivered Notices as if it had been applied once.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana Ruiz registered with ana@example.org and has the cordless drill on loan L1, due 12 October. Ben Ito registered with ben@example.org, and Hold Fulfilled was recorded for his hold H1 on the hedge trimmer with a collect-by date of 16 October.

  • Overdue notice fails (INV-UDN-1, INV-UDN-2, INV-UDN-3)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices is empty
    • When: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1 on 13 October, as bounced
    • Then: Undelivered Notices lists an overdue-notice entry: Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, the cordless drill, due 12 October, failed 13 October, bounced.
  • Due date shown after an extension (INV-UDN-3)
    • Given: Loan Extended moved L1's due date to 19 October, and the loan is now overdue
    • When: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1 on 20 October, as refused
    • Then: the entry shows the due date 19 October, failed 20 October, refused.
  • Pickup notice fails (INV-UDN-1, INV-UDN-2, INV-UDN-3a)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry
    • When: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1 on 13 October, as refused
    • Then: Undelivered Notices also lists a pickup-notice entry: Ben Ito, ben@example.org, the hedge trimmer, collect by 16 October, failed 13 October, refused. Ana's entry is unchanged.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-UDN-8)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry once
    • When: the same Overdue Notice Failed for L1 is applied again
    • Then: the entry is still listed once.
  • Tool returned (INV-UDN-4)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry for L1
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1
    • Then: Ana's entry drops off.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-UDN-4)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry for L1
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L1
    • Then: Ana's entry drops off.
  • Tool retired while out (INV-UDN-4)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry for L1
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the cordless drill
    • Then: Ana's entry stays. It drops off once L1 is returned or recorded lost.
  • Holder collects the tool (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the hedge trimmer and Ben
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Someone else checks out the tool (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1, and his collect-by date has passed, but Hold Expired hasn't been recorded
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the hedge trimmer and Cara
    • Then: Ben's entry stays until Hold Expired is recorded for H1, and then drops off.
  • Holder cancels the hold (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Set-aside expires (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Tool retired while set aside (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the hedge trimmer
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ben
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Neighbor corrects their email (INV-UDN-3)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry, showing ana@example.org, the address that bounced
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: Ana's entry shows ana.ruiz@example.net. The entry stays until L1 is returned or recorded lost.
  • Listing undelivered notices
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry and Ben's pickup-notice entry
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists undelivered notices
    • Then: both entries are returned with all their fields, with no paging.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-UDN-8). An event applied a second time leaves the entries as they were after the first.
  • Ended loans and set-asides: a failure report for a loan or set-aside that has already ended is ignored by Record Overdue Notice Failure and Record Pickup Notice Failure, so no entry is ever created for one. An entry, once it drops off, never comes back.
  • No actions: the screen issues no commands, so it has no refusals. Its only use is to prompt the shed manager to follow up in person.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Undelivered Notices screen is the shed manager's alone; neighbors never see it. How the system recognises the shed manager is the open identity question in Add Tool (slices/add-tool.md); this view follows its answer.
  • PII & compliance: shows neighbors' names, current emails and the tools they have or are waiting for, to the shed manager only. An entry is kept only while its loan or set-aside is live. How long personal data is kept in general is the shed-wide personal-data question in .event-modeling.md (Open questions).
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Overdue Notice Failed (Record Overdue Notice Failure): loanId, reason, failedAt.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (Record Pickup Notice Failure): holdId, reason, failedAt.
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool), Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, collectByDate.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs. Hold Fulfilled carrying toolId and neighborId is this view's assumption, because it doesn't hear Hold Placed; Fulfill Hold is checked against it when it is written in depth.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen issues no commands.

Open Questions

  • How a person is recognised (the identity question) — brief 10 A1. Only the shed manager may see this screen.
  • List order — brief 10 A4.
  • How long personal data is kept — brief 11 B7. This screen shows neighbors' names and emails.
